- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. The flow for another user's profile image request:
- Browser requests `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`
- Handler `serveUserAvatar` at line 168 of fileserver.go resolves the username
- Calls `getUserByUsername` at line 715 which queries the database
- Database driver (SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL) executes SELECT query including `avatar_url` column at lines 159 (SQLite), 150 (PostgreSQL), 147 (MySQL)
- User data with avatar_url is returned to the handler
- Handler parses the data URI at line 737 using `parseDataURI`
- Image data is decoded from base64 and returned as response
